title: Wingy's rehearsal bands, Loyacano brothers, Cinderella Ballroom and other Chicago jobs
summary: Rinker recalls Wingy's rehearsal bands, jobbing with Jack and Deacon Loyacano at the Cinderella around 1927, Larry Tice and Bix, Jules Bufano, Pecora, the Arcadia with Husk O'Hare-type bands opposite Elgar, and Midway Gardens.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I was in and I think Max Kaminsky was the other trumpet in it. I think Marty Marcel was the other trumpet at one time. Floyd O'Brien was in it. Uh I think uh uh most everybody was in it that was around and once in a while we'd play a job sometimes we wouldn't. Wingy had uh a job in that ballroom at uh Sheffield and uh Belmont. Uh did he have that job in this period? About that time. Yeah. But I wasn't in the band. I don't think I may have been. Come to think of it I did play there or some play. I played in some ballroom with him a little bit. It wasn't much of a job. I think it was two or three nights a week and it lasted a little while. And Wingy was in front of the band and he would he would play a chorus now and then and sing. There was Jack Loicano uh uh and he had a brother Deacon Loicano. They called him Deacon. Uh Jack played trombone and uh Deacon played string bass. And I played with both of them a great deal. This was mainly a jobbing uh Jobbing mainly. Sometime I think I played a steady job or two with the Deacon Loicano. One of the chop suey places probably. Might have been Cinderella. Cinderella Ballroom I know I played did play with him. That was a 10 or 11 piece band. Would you be able to guess the date? 1926 to 28 and through there. 27 probably. 1927. I think Bernard Dixon was in the, Dick Dixon was in the band. But where, what was the location of Cinderella? It was on uh around 63rd and Cottage. It was right across the street about a block from the trianon. And they uh they always had a band of eight to 10 or 11 pieces there. I played there with I believe three different leaders three different times. And that was when I was playing at the trianon and then at the little uh chop suey place at the corner of 63rd and uh 63rd and Cottage. I played there sometimes too. Sterling Bowes used to come there. And uh this saxophone player I was trying to mention uh the other night was Larry Tice. He used to come there and set in with us regular in this little place at 63rd and Cottage at the corner. He knew Bix by the way. He knew him quite well. Larry did. Yes certainly. He wanted me to go with him one night to uh see Bix and for some reason I didn't go. I don't know why it was. That was in the later, that was not too long before Bix went to New York and uh was killed or died. That's right it was Rod that fell down wasn't it? Bix died of lower pneumonia. But I remember that time Larry came by for me. It was raining or something and uh I didn't go with him. I should have. I used to go to the trianon and hear uh little Sterling play. He played very well. Is he still alive? Do you know? No. That was Jules Cassard. He used to play string bass mostly but two but some and I played with him quite a bit. I can't remember just where. Columbia Ballroom I think and other places. Jules Bufano, he's now with uh as far as I know with uh Jimmy Durante. I played a great deal with him with the Benson organization and uh we had a band together for a while. He was a very good bass player. He is still. Sandals Pecora, trombone. I played with him some good trombone player. There are others. I just can't remember them now. A lot of them I mentioned the other night. But these are some that I had forgotten and I thought that you ought to know about. I have to mention John that during the days that the Arcadia Ballroom was open I used to play with Husker Harris Orchestra there and I played opposite uh Elgar's orchestra quite a bit. We were a regular feature there. That would be in 1925, 26, 27 and 28 and through there and I think I played opposite Cook there later or earlier. I've forgotten which. There are also some color musicians that used to have a second band at the Midway. After Muggsy left there I went there with Mel Stitzel and then again with Floyd Towne.
